english.notes:
(i) See also offence wordings: H1801, H1802 and H1803.
(ii) Section 5(1)(b) of the Firearms Act 1968 provides: "Any weapon of whatever description designed or adapted for the discharge of any noxious liquid, gas or other thing". This includes electrical incapacitation devices such as stun guns and "tazers". The emission of electricity from a stun device amounts to a 'discharge' and a "Lightning Strike" hand-held electric stun device was held to be a weapon designed for the discharge of a noxious thing (see Flack v Baldry [1988] 1 All ER 673)).
(iii) Cattle prods are not considered to be within this category as they are not designed or adapted as weapons.
(iv) The unlawful discharge of a gas which is being used as a weapon (e.g. CS sprays), is different from compressed carbon dioxide which can be used to propel a pellet from an air weapon.
(v) On conviction for this offence, the court can order the forfeiture or disposal of any firearm or ammunition and cancellation of any firearm certificate or shot gun certificate, and any firearm or ammunition subject of such order may be seized or detained by a constable (section 52 of the Firearms Act 1968).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.
